plans.label: Transplanted
prevent: Sow clean seed. Weedy rice and grass seeds come in with farm saved seed, so buy certified seed, or float your own seed in water, skim off what floats and pick out red, awned or odd grains.
Prepare the land twice. Flood and plow, wait 7 to 10 days for the weed seeds to sprout, then harrow them under. A second wait and harrowing before planting kills a second flush (the stale seedbed).
Level the field so one depth of water covers every part. High spots grow weeds and low spots drown the young rice.
Keep the seedbed, bunds and canals clean, and wash the tractor, harrow and thresher before they come in from a weedy field.
Transplant sturdy seedlings at even spacing in straight rows, so the rice starts taller than the weeds and a rotary weeder can pass.
Pull escapes, weedy rice above all, before they flower; one plant that drops its seed fills the field next season.
Switch herbicide groups from season to season so the weeds do not learn to survive one group.

rice.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 10 to 40 days after transplanting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: 0 to 5 days
windows.stage: Before the weeds come up
steps: Keep the soil saturated, or under 2 to 3 cm of water, from the day you transplant. Water over the soil stops most grass seeds from sprouting.
Replant missing hills now, so the gaps do not fill with weeds.

If this field had a lot of weeds last season, apply a pre emergence herbicide now, before the weeds come up, and keep the water in for 3 to 5 days so it does not wash away. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
windows.title: 0 to 5 days after transplanting

windows.label: 6 to 10 days
windows.stage: Weeds at two to three leaves
steps: Pull the weeds by hand while they are small and easy to tell from the rice.

Where you cannot weed by hand, spray an early post emergence herbicide on weeds at 2 to 3 leaves. Drain the field to wet mud first if the label says so. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water. Keep the young rice above it.
windows.title: 6 to 10 days after transplanting

windows.label: 11 to 20 days
windows.stage: Weeds growing with the rice
steps: Keep water in the field. It stops weed seeds from sprouting and holds back the seedlings that already did.
Run a rotary weeder between the rows at about 15 days, and pull what grows inside the hills. It cuts, tramples and buries the weeds and loosens the soil for the roots.
Let nature help. Grow Azolla on the water, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats the leaves of Ludwigia weeds.
If weeding cannot keep up, apply a post emergence herbicide. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water. Keep the young rice above it.
windows.title: 11 to 20 days after transplanting

windows.label: 21 to 30 days
windows.stage: Rice tillering
steps: Top up the water if the level has dropped.
Give the rotary weeder a second pass about 10 days after the first, before the rice closes over the rows; later passes break the tillers.
Let nature help. Grow Azolla on the water, and spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats the leaves of Ludwigia weeds.

2,4 D and MCPA belong here, once the rice has tillered; on younger rice they can twist the leaves. If weeding cannot keep up, apply a post emergence herbicide. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water.
windows.title: 21 to 30 days after transplanting

windows.label: 31 to 40 days
windows.stage: Rice near full tillering
steps: Top up the water if the level has dropped.
Pull the weeds by hand, grasses and weedy rice first, before they flower.
Spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats the leaves of Ludwigia weeds.
Spray only as a rescue, when weeding has failed. Use a post emergence herbicide and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
windows.title: 31 to 40 days after transplanting

plans.label: Direct seeded
prevent: Sow clean seed. Weedy rice and grass seeds come in with farm saved seed, so buy certified seed, or float your own seed in water, skim off what floats and pick out red, awned or odd grains.
Prepare the land twice. Flood and plow, wait 7 to 10 days for the weed seeds to sprout, then harrow them under. A second wait and harrowing before planting kills a second flush (the stale seedbed).
Level the field so one depth of water covers every part. High spots grow weeds and low spots drown the young rice.
Sow pregerminated seed on a firm, level seedbed at the seeding rate your seed calls for. A thick, even stand shades out weeds sooner than a thin one.
Weedy rice spreads fastest in direct seeding. Where it is bad, transplant for a season or two, or sow in rows so you can tell the crop from the weed.
Keep the seedbed, bunds and canals clean, and wash the tractor, harrow and thresher before they come in from a weedy field.
Pull escapes, weedy rice above all, before they flower; one plant that drops its seed fills the field next season.
Switch herbicide groups from season to season so the weeds do not learn to survive one group.

rice.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 14 to 50 days after seeding; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: 0 to 5 days
windows.stage: Before the weeds come up
steps: Keep the soil saturated after seeding, with no standing water until the seedlings are up. Wet soil holds back many weed seeds.

If this field had a lot of weeds last season, apply a pre emergence herbicide now, before the weeds come up. In wet seeded rice, use one made for it, such as pretilachlor with a safener. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
windows.title: 0 to 5 days after seeding

windows.label: 6 to 10 days
windows.stage: Weeds at two to three leaves
steps: Spray an early post emergence herbicide while the weeds are still at 2 to 3 leaves. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water. Keep the young rice above it.
Where you sowed in rows, a light hoe or push weeder between the rows works from now on.
windows.title: 6 to 10 days after seeding

windows.label: 11 to 20 days
windows.stage: Weeds growing with the rice
steps: Keep water in the field once the rice can take it, 2 to 5 cm deep. It stops weed seeds from sprouting and holds back the seedlings that already did.
Pull the weeds by hand, or hoe between the rows where you sowed in lines. Fill thin spots, where weeds take over first.
Spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats the leaves of Ludwigia weeds.
If hand weeding cannot keep up, apply a post emergence herbicide. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water. Keep the young rice above it.
windows.title: 11 to 20 days after seeding

windows.label: 21 to 30 days
windows.stage: Rice tillering
steps: Top up the water if the level has dropped.
Pull the weeds by hand, grasses and weedy rice first, before the rice closes over the ground.
Spare the small black Altica beetle, which eats the leaves of Ludwigia weeds.
2,4 D and MCPA belong here, once the rice has tillered. If hand weeding cannot keep up, apply a post emergence herbicide. Read and follow the label on the bottle, box or sachet.
Bring the water back 1 to 3 days after you spray, 3 to 5 cm deep, and hold it there for 4 to 5 days so the weeds stay under water.
windows.title: 21 to 30 days after seeding

plans.label: Corn and sorghum
prevent: Plow and harrow twice, about 2 weeks apart. The first flush of weeds, itchgrass among them, sprouts after the first pass and dies at the second.
Plant on time, at the spacing your seed calls for, with a full stand. Corn that comes up evenly shades the rows about 6 weeks after planting.
Put the fertilizer in the furrow or beside the hill, not spread over the whole field, so it feeds the corn and not the weeds.
Clean the harrow, planter and sheller after a weedy field so itchgrass seed does not travel to the next one.
Rotate with mungbean or peanut, and do not let the weeds between seasons go to seed.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 6 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Field being plowed, or green weeds before no till planting
steps: Plow and harrow, then let the next flush of weeds come up and harrow again just before you plant (the stale seedbed).
For no till planting, or where cogon and other perennial grasses grow, spray a burndown herbicide on green, growing weeds 7 to 14 days before planting.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after planting
windows.stage: Seed in the ground; corn and weeds not up yet
steps: Spray a pre emergence herbicide on moist soil right after planting, before the corn and the weeds come up. Do not walk on the sprayed soil afterwards.
A pre emergence spray, then hilling up at about 25 days, keeps itchgrass and most other weeds down until the corn shades them.
Sorghum takes atrazine; most other corn herbicides injure it.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after planting

windows.label: 2 to 4 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Corn at 3 to 6 leaves; weeds at 2 to 4 leaves
steps: Keep the field weed free from 2 to 6 weeks after planting; weeds cut corn yield most in these weeks.
Off bar about 2 weeks after planting and hill up at about 25 to 30 days, then pull the weeds left in the row by hand.
If you spray, spray small weeds. Glyphosate goes over the top only of corn whose seed bag says it is herbicide tolerant. 2,4 D can injure sweet corn.
grasses: Mesotrione plus glyphosate plus S metolachlor (herbicide tolerant corn only)
sedges: Mesotrione plus glyphosate plus S metolachlor (herbicide tolerant corn only)
broadleaves: Mesotrione plus glyphosate plus S metolachlor (herbicide tolerant corn only)
windows.title: 2 to 4 weeks after planting

windows.label: 4 to 6 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Corn knee high; rows not closed yet
steps: Hill up if you have not, and pull or slash weeds in the rows before they flower. One itchgrass plant drops thousands of seeds, so never let it set seed.
Use only directed sprays now: hold the nozzle low between the rows with a shield and never let the spray touch the corn leaves.
Once the rows close, the corn shades out most new weeds; pull the big ones that are left before harvest.
windows.title: 4 to 6 weeks after planting

plans.label: Legumes, beans and cotton
prevent: Pick the field with the fewest weeds. Beans have few herbicides labelled for them here, so a clean start counts double.
Prepare the land well, then let the weeds sprout for a week and harrow once more before planting (the stale seedbed). After rice, plant into the stubble as soon as you can, before weeds start.
Sow good seed at a close, even spacing; beans grow slowly in their first weeks and a full stand covers the ground sooner.
Mulch with rice straw after planting in fields that cannot be cultivated; 3 to 5 cm of straw holds back most weeds.
Do not let weeds seed at the field edges or between seasons.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 6 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

mungbean.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 14 to 30 days after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

peanut.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 3 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

pigeonpea.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

cotton.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Field being prepared, or rice stubble after harvest
steps: Plow and harrow, wait about a week for the weeds to sprout, then harrow once more just before planting.
For zero tillage after rice, spray the weeds and stubble with a burndown herbicide 3 to 7 days before dibbling the seed.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after planting
windows.stage: Seed sown; crop and weeds not up yet
steps: Spray a pre emergence herbicide on moist soil within 3 days after planting, before the crop and the weeds come up.
Purple nutsedge sprouts from tubers that sprays here do not reach; plow it out before planting and pull what comes back.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after planting

windows.label: 2 to 4 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Crop at 2 to 4 leaves; first flush of weeds
steps: Weed control matters most 2 to 4 weeks after the crop comes up. About 15 days after planting, off bar between rows, hand weed what is left, then hill up right away. A second weeding about 2 weeks later finishes the job for most beans.
Hill up peanut before the pegs go into the soil, not after, so you do not break them.
Grass killers are safe over the top of beans and cotton but do nothing to sedges or broadleaves.
windows.title: 2 to 4 weeks after planting

windows.label: 4 to 6 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Crop flowering or pegging; leaves closing over the rows
steps: Stop cultivating once peanut starts pegging and beans flower; spot weed by hand instead.
Directed sprays fit only tall or trellised crops such as cotton, pigeon pea and string bean: shield the nozzle and keep the spray off the leaves.
Pull weeds before they seed so they do not fill the next crop, and keep to the waiting days before harvest on the label.
windows.title: 4 to 6 weeks after planting

plans.label: Root and tuber crops
prevent: Plow, harrow and ridge the field, and pick out cogon and nutsedge runners and tubers by hand as you go; every piece left grows back.
Plant clean cuttings, setts and seed pieces, and plant them at a close, even spacing so the leaves cover the ground early.
Mulch ginger, turmeric, ubi and upland taro right after planting with rice straw, dried grass or coconut fronds; for these crops mulch and the hoe do most of the work.
Intercrop cassava with corn, peanut or mungbean in its first months; the second crop covers the ground the cassava leaves open.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 6 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

cassava.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 4 to 12 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

taro.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 3 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

ubi.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 4 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

ginger.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 4 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

turmeric.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 4 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Field being cleared, plowed and ridged
steps: Where cogon or other perennial grass covers the land, spray it with glyphosate while green and growing, then plow 2 weeks later when it browns.
Let a flush of weeds sprout after plowing and harrow them under before you ridge and plant.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after planting
windows.stage: Cuttings, setts or seed pieces just planted; no weeds up
steps: Cassava grows slowly and loses most to weeds in its first 3 months; a pre emergence spray right after planting holds the first weeds back.
In potato, spray after planting and before the sprouts break the soil.
Few herbicides are labelled for sweet potato, taro, ubi, ginger and turmeric here; mulch them and plan to hoe.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after planting

windows.label: 3 to 8 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Crop leafing out; first weeds growing between rows
steps: Hand weed or hoe at about 3 to 4 weeks and again at 6 to 8 weeks; cassava needs at least two weedings, and a third at about 12 weeks, before its leaves shade the ground.
Hill up potato and sweet potato about a month after planting; hilling buries the small weeds. Top up thin mulch on ginger, turmeric and ubi.
Weed sweet potato before the vines run; once they cover the ground, they hold the weeds back on their own.
windows.title: 3 to 8 weeks after planting

windows.label: 2 months after planting until the leaves cover the ground
windows.stage: Vines running or canopy closing; roots and tubers swelling
steps: Pull the big weeds by hand; do not dig near swelling roots and tubers.
Between wide cassava rows, slash the weeds or use a directed spray with a shield, and keep it off the green stems and leaves.
Once the canopy covers the ground, shade does most of the work.
windows.title: 2 months after planting until the leaves cover the ground

plans.label: Fruit vegetables, cabbages and gourds
prevent: Make the beds, water them and wait 1 to 2 weeks for the weed seeds to sprout, then rake or scrape them off shallowly and plant without digging again (the stale seedbed).
Lay plastic mulch, silver side up, over the beds before transplanting; it stops most weeds in the bed. Kill purple nutsedge first, because its shoots pierce the plastic.
On beds without plastic, rice straw, rice hull or coco coir dust 3 to 5 cm thick holds back weeds and keeps the soil moist.
Use well rotted compost and manure; fresh manure carries live weed seeds.
Transplant strong seedlings, so the crop starts weeks ahead of the weeds.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 6 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

eggplant.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

chili.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 9 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

bellpepper.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 9 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

cabbage.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

broccoli.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

cauliflower.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

celery.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

ampalaya.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

squash.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

cucumber.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

patola.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

upo.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

watermelon.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

melon.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

sayote.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 3 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

strawberry.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Beds being made; mulch not laid yet
steps: Make the beds and let the first weeds sprout, then rake or spray them off before you plant (the stale seedbed).
Burndown sprays are only for weeds before the beds are made or the mulch is laid, never on the crop.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after planting
windows.stage: Seedlings just set out or seed just sown; weeds not up
steps: On unmulched beds and in the paths, a pre emergence herbicide on moist soil holds weeds for the first weeks. Spray before transplanting, or on the soil only after it, as the label says.
Squash, gourds, melons and okra sown from seed are easily hurt; spray only the paths between their rows.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after planting

windows.label: 2 to 4 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Plants setting new leaves; vines starting to run
steps: Pull weeds in the planting holes by hand. In unmulched fields, off bar about 2 weeks after planting and hill up a week later, then pull the weeds left in the row.
Weed gourds and melons before the vines run; after that, the vines cover the ground but are easily torn.
Grass killers are safe over the top of these crops. For broadleaves and sedges in the paths, use only a shielded spray.
windows.title: 2 to 4 weeks after planting

windows.label: 4 weeks after planting until harvest
windows.stage: Flowering and fruiting; leaves or vines covering the beds
steps: Stop deep cultivation once fruits set so you do not cut the roots; hand weed instead.
Slash the paths, or spray them with a shield; never let drift reach leaves or fruit, and keep to the waiting days before harvest on the label.
Keep field edges clean; weeds there carry insects and viruses into the crop.
windows.title: 4 weeks after planting until harvest

plans.label: Onion, garlic and shallot
prevent: Onion and garlic leaves shade almost nothing, so they lose to weeds more than any other crop. Start with the cleanest field you have.
In plowed fields, let the weeds sprout for a week or two between passes and plow again; repeated tillage wears down purple nutsedge, the hardest weed here.
After rice, cut the stubble low and plant into it with zero tillage, then cover the beds with 5 cm of rice straw; the straw holds weeds and keeps the soil moist.
Plant clean sets, cloves and seedlings, free of weed seed and soil from weedy beds.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 10 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

shallot.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

onion_spring.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 5 weeks after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Rice stubble after harvest, or a plowed field
steps: After rice, spray the weeds and volunteer rice with a burndown herbicide before planting with zero tillage.
In onion, oxyfluorfen can go on the bed before transplanting, as its label says.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after planting
windows.stage: Sets, cloves or seedlings just planted; weeds not up
steps: Spray a pre emergence herbicide on moist soil right after planting, then cover the beds with rice straw mulch.
Oxyfluorfen before emergence can thin the stand of some onion varieties; try it on a small area first.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after planting

windows.label: 2 to 5 weeks after planting
windows.stage: Crop at 2 to 5 leaves; first flush of weeds
steps: Hand weed at about 3 weeks and again at 5 to 6 weeks; keep the beds clean until the bulbs form.
Oxyfluorfen and pendimethalin can go over onion once it has 2 true leaves or more, on small weeds only.
Grass killers take out grasses and volunteer rice; purple nutsedge has to be pulled.
grasses: Pendimethalin (crop at 2 true leaves or more)
sedges: Oxyfluorfen (crop at 2 true leaves or more)
broadleaves: Oxyfluorfen (crop at 2 true leaves or more)
Pendimethalin (crop at 2 true leaves or more)
windows.title: 2 to 5 weeks after planting

windows.label: 6 weeks after planting until harvest
windows.stage: Bulbs forming; leaves full grown
steps: Pull weeds by hand and do not hoe deep near the bulbs.
Grass killers still work on grasses; keep to the waiting days before harvest on the label.
Spring onion is pulled young: hand weed it and skip sprays near harvest.
windows.title: 6 weeks after planting until harvest

plans.label: Leafy greens, carrot and radish
prevent: Make the beds, water them and wait 7 to 10 days for weeds to sprout, then scrape them off shallowly and sow without digging again (the stale seedbed).
Use well rotted compost; raw manure carries weed seeds.
Sow in rows, not broadcast, so you can weed between them, and mulch the paths with rice straw or rice hull.
For lowland kangkong, a steady water level holds back most weeds.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 3 weeks after sowing; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

carrot.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 2 to 8 weeks after sowing; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

radish.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 4 weeks after sowing; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before sowing
windows.stage: Beds being prepared
steps: Let the first weeds sprout on the new beds, then scrape them off and sow (the stale seedbed).
A burndown spray is only for weeds before the beds are made.
windows.title: Before sowing

windows.label: 0 to 3 days after sowing
windows.stage: Seed sown; nothing up yet
steps: Kangkong, lettuce, alugbati and saluyot have no herbicide labelled for them here; sow in rows, mulch the paths and plan to hand weed.
Carrot can take a pre emergence spray right after sowing, before it comes up.
Oxadiazon is labelled here for cabbage and the other crucifers; on pechay and mustard sown from seed, try it on a small bed first.
windows.title: 0 to 3 days after sowing

windows.label: 1 to 3 weeks after sowing
windows.stage: Seedlings at 2 to 4 leaves; weeds sprouting in the rows
steps: Thin the seedlings and pull weeds at the same time, then hand weed again a week or two later.
Close spacing helps the crop shade the soil sooner.
In carrot, linuron on small weeds is the only spray; leafy greens are hand weeded.
windows.title: 1 to 3 weeks after sowing

windows.label: 3 weeks after sowing until harvest
windows.stage: Leaves covering the bed; harvest near
steps: Pull the remaining weeds gently by hand so you do not loosen the crop.
Do not spray herbicide on leafy greens; people eat the leaves.
Clear the paths and edges so weeds do not seed the next planting.
windows.title: 3 weeks after sowing until harvest

plans.label: Sugarcane
prevent: Plow, harrow and furrow well, and kill cogon, talahib and purple nutsedge before planting; they are hard to remove from standing cane.
Plant healthy setts close enough for a full stand, and fill the gaps within a month; gaps are where the weeds come in.
In ratoons, leave the cane trash on the rows as mulch; it holds back many weeds.
Cut climbing vines such as morning glory and mile a minute before they seed or pull the cane down.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 4 months after planting or ratooning; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Field plowed and furrowed; old cane or grass to clear
steps: Spray perennial grass with glyphosate while it is green and growing, then plow 2 weeks later.
Let a flush of weeds sprout after plowing and harrow them under before you furrow.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 5 days after planting or ratooning
windows.stage: Setts planted or cane just cut; cane and weeds not up
steps: Spray a pre emergence herbicide on moist soil right after planting, or right after the ratoon is cleaned up, before the weeds come up.
Where purple nutsedge is the main weed, pick an ingredient that names it on the label.
windows.title: 0 to 5 days after planting or ratooning

windows.label: 3 to 8 weeks after planting or ratooning
windows.stage: Cane tillering; weeds small
steps: Spray small weeds early; ametryn and 2,4 D go over young cane, but read the label for the cane age limit.
Off bar and cultivate between rows about 4 to 6 weeks after planting; it buries weeds and loosens the soil.
Itchgrass and nutsedge come in flushes; a second spray or cultivation 3 to 4 weeks later stops the next one.
windows.title: 3 to 8 weeks after planting or ratooning

windows.label: 2 to 4 months after planting
windows.stage: Cane knee to waist high; rows not closed
steps: Hill up and weed by hand or with an animal drawn cultivator before the rows close.
Use only directed sprays between the rows, with a shield, and keep them off the cane leaves.
Pull or cut morning glory and other vines before they climb the stalks.
windows.title: 2 to 4 months after planting

windows.label: 4 months after planting until harvest
windows.stage: Rows closed; cane shades the ground
steps: The closed canopy shades out most weeds. Walk the field and cut climbing vines such as morning glory and mile a minute before they pull the cane down.
Treat patches of cogon or talahib after harvest, not in standing cane.
windows.title: 4 months after planting until harvest

plans.label: Pineapple
prevent: Plow, harrow and bed the field, and kill cogon and nutsedge before planting; they are hard to remove later.
Plant through plastic mulch where you can, or mulch the beds with dried grass; pineapple is slow to cover the ground.
Plant crowns and suckers of one size together, so the field closes evenly.

*.say: Keep the field free of weeds from about 1 to 6 months after planting; weeds cost the most yield in that stretch.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Field plowed and bedded; old crop chopped
steps: Kill standing cogon and other perennial weeds with a burndown herbicide while they are green, then plow and bed.
If you use plastic mulch, lay it on the beds and plant through it.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: 0 to 7 days after planting
windows.stage: Crowns or suckers just planted; soil bare
steps: Spray a pre emergence herbicide over the newly planted field on moist soil. Bromacil with diuron is the usual plantation practice here.
These herbicides hold weeds for about 2 to 3 months; repeat only as the label allows.
windows.title: 0 to 7 days after planting

windows.label: 1 to 4 months after planting
windows.stage: Plants rooting and putting out leaves; weeds between beds
steps: Hand weed or hoe the paths between beds, and pull weeds out of the plant hearts carefully.
Ametryn and diuron can go over young pineapple to kill small weeds and hold new ones. Never spray glyphosate on pineapple.
Keep the field clean until the leaves cover the ground; weeds cost pineapple the most yield in its first 6 months.
windows.title: 1 to 4 months after planting

windows.label: 5 months after planting to forcing, and ratoons
windows.stage: Leaves cover most of the ground
steps: Spot weed by hand; keep vines and tall grasses out of the field.
In ratoon crops, clean the paths after harvest and apply a pre emergence herbicide again as the label allows.
A grass killer goes over the plants for grasses only; any other spray goes on the paths, never on pineapple leaves.
windows.title: 5 months after planting to forcing, and ratoons

plans.label: Plantations and fruit trees
prevent: Clear the brush and slash the grass, but do not burn; burning destroys the organic matter in the soil.
Sow a legume cover crop such as Centrosema, Calopogonium or Pueraria between the rows as soon as the land is cleared; a good cover replaces cogon within a few months.
Grow short crops such as sweet potato, peanut, ginger or upland rice between young trees; they pay their way and keep the ground covered.
Mulch the ring around each young plant with cut grass, leaves, coconut husk or rice hull.
Cut out Siam weed, lantana and other shrubs, and pull climbing vines, before they seed.

*.say: Keep a clean ring around every young plant for its first 2 to 3 years, and weed young banana and papaya most carefully in their first 6 months.

windows.label: Before planting
windows.stage: Land being cleared; cogon or brush on the field
steps: Kill cogon and other perennial grass with glyphosate while it is green and growing, then plant 2 to 4 weeks later.
Sow the cover crop between the rows right after clearing, before the weeds come back.
windows.title: Before planting

windows.label: First 1 to 3 years after planting
windows.stage: Young plants; sunlight reaches the ground between them
steps: Ring weed a circle around each plant before every fertilizer application: about 60 to 75 cm wide for banana and 1 m for cacao, wider as trees grow. Slash the rows between plants every 2 to 3 months.
Mulch the rings with cut grass, leaves or rice hull, and keep the cover crop or intercrop growing between the rows.

Keep every spray off green stems, young bark, leaves and suckers. Banana, papaya and dragon fruit take up glyphosate through their green skin; hand weed young banana until about 6 months. Cacao does best with slashing and mulch, not herbicide.
grasses: Fluazifop P butyl (grasses in cover crops)
windows.title: First 1 to 3 years after planting

windows.label: Established and bearing trees
windows.stage: Trees bearing; shade covers part of the ground
steps: Keep a clean ring around each trunk and slash the rest of the field 3 to 4 times a year. Cover crops, or animals grazing under coconut, also keep the grass down.
Cut and pull climbing vines such as mile a minute and stinking passion flower, and cut out Siam weed, lantana and other shrubs before they seed.
Spot spray the rings and paths only, never the leaves, fruit or green bark; banana and papaya are hurt by any drift that touches them. Glyphosate is the one for cogon.
grasses: Fluazifop P butyl (grasses in cover crops)
windows.title: Established and bearing trees
